message.content: {"caption":"A two-part figure showing an experience-to-skills pipeline and success rates for three methods over training steps.","description":"Panel (a) is a process diagram. A Base Model robot interacts with the Environment through a loop of arrows, and an arrow leads from the Environment to a branching Trajectory. The trajectory separates into successful episodes, marked by a green check, and failed episodes, marked by a red X; solid colored arrows carry these experiences to an Expert, shown as a document. The Expert sends an orange arrow to Memory, depicted as a stack of items, and Memory points right to Skills, depicted as a folder containing reusable skills. Gray dashed routes show the alternative of sending raw successful trajectories directly to Memory and failed ones to Discard, shown as a bin. Beneath Skills, a red circular-arrow symbol labeled Evolve sits between robot icons, indicating an evolution loop involving the agent and its skills. Panel (b) is a line chart with Training Steps on the x-axis (0–150) and Success Rate (%) on the y-axis (0–100). The legend identifies Vanilla GRPO (blue solid line), GRPO+Memory (gray dashed line), and SkillRL (Ours; red solid line). All three start near 10%. SkillRL rises fastest, reaches about 80% around 40 steps, and then stays near 90%; Vanilla GRPO and GRPO+Memory increase more gradually and remain lower, ending at roughly 75% and 60%, respectively. A star marks SkillRL near 74 steps and 90%, a triangle marks GRPO+Memory near 91 steps and 63%, and a square marks Vanilla GRPO near 105 steps and 74%; each has a vertical dashed guide. An inset with icons labels the comparisons “Higher Performance” and “Faster Convergence.” The plotted point values below are estimated from the axes; the chart does not print individual data
